member.name: T:Storeasy.Application.Interfaces.ISecurityStampStore
member.summary: Per-user revocation stamp store. The stamp is the source of truth for "are this user's tokens still valid": it is baked into the access token at login and checked on every request. Backed by Redis for a cheap per-request read, with the database (User.SessionStamp) as the durable source of truth and a fail-safe fallback when Redis is unavailable.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Interfaces.ISecurityStampStore.GetOrCreateAsync(System.Int32,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Returns the user's current stamp, creating and persisting one if the user has none yet. Used when minting a token so the token always carries a valid stamp.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Interfaces.ISecurityStampStore.RotateAsync(System.Int32,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Rotates the user's stamp (new value persisted to the database and written through to the cache), instantly invalidating every access token that carried the old stamp. Called on password change, role change, lock and deletion. Call it after the transaction that revokes the sessions has committed (never inside it), so a concurrent request can never re-cache the old stamp.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Interfaces.ISecurityStampStore.IsValidAsync(System.Int32,System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Validates a stamp presented by a token against the user's current stamp (Redis, with a database fallback). Returns true when they match.

member.name: T:Storeasy.Application.Interfaces.ITransactionRunner
member.summary:
Runs a unit of database work inside a real transaction that the transaction interceptor opens on the (proxied) implementation. Handlers use this to keep ONLY their DB mutations transactional while doing external work (cache writes, notifications, e-mail) AFTER the commit, instead of wrapping the whole handler in [Transaction] (which would drag those external calls inside the transaction).
Milvasoft interception is proxy-based, so the transaction only fires when the method is invoked through this injected interface. A private [Transaction] method on the handler itself would NOT open a transaction: a same-instance call bypasses the proxy (self-invocation), so the interceptor never runs.

member.name: M:Storeasy.Application.Interfaces.ITransactionRunner.RunAsync(System.Func{System.Threading.Tasks.Task})
member.summary: Runs inside a transaction: commits when it completes, rolls back if it throws. Only put database mutations in ; do external calls after this returns.
member.param: The database work to run transactionally.

member.summary: Builds every Redis key of the application, always as {prefix}:{key} with the prefix of , so applications that share one Redis never read or overwrite each other's entries (revocation stamps, rate limit counters, the feature flag cache). member.remarks: A service that must reach another application's keys on purpose (an admin API that revokes the tokens of the main API's users) creates a second instance with that application's options instead of repeating the key format.
